directFoodUseException: An edible Food-group good with a positive Hunger consumption effect may have direct eating as its only use. Ingredient oils, juvenile stock, fertilizers and service tokens are not exempt.
definition: Distinct useful downstream products, building construction, consumption or services. Storage, transport, disposal, alternate recipes for the same product and self-recycling do not add uses.

singleUseExceptions.RocketAirframe: Rocket-specific final-goal component, explicitly exempted by the user.
singleUseExceptions.PropulsionPackage: Rocket-specific final-goal component, explicitly exempted by the user.
singleUseExceptions.MissionPayload: Rocket-specific final-goal payload, explicitly exempted by the user.
singleUseExceptions.RadioactiveSludge: Waste product shown as Radioactive Water: its destination is disposal (Radioactive Waste Export off the map, or the Outfall into a river). Vitrification and mineral recovery were removed with the user's 2026-10-29 simplification of the waste chain.

legacySaveOnlyGoods.IndustrialLicense: Retired 2026-10-21: Technical School courses now train persistent specialists (tools/workforce_risks.json). The good stays defined, unproduced and unused, only so existing saves that hold it still load.
legacySaveOnlyGoods.SpecialistLicense: Retired 2026-10-21 with IndustrialLicense; unproduced and unused, kept only for saves.
legacySaveOnlyGoods.FlightLicense: Retired 2026-10-21 with IndustrialLicense; Mission Control no longer makes it. Unproduced and unused, kept only for saves.
legacySaveOnlyGoods.RecoveredMinerals: Retired 2026-10-29 (user decision): waste refining no longer yields minerals, mineral recovery is removed and the reactor's 10-mineral gate became 100 extra HighGradeSteel. The good stays defined, unproduced and unused, only so saves that hold it still load.
legacySaveOnlyGoods.Lubricant: Retired 2026-10-30 (user decision: "the vanilla game has grease. lets use it."): every use moved to the vanilla Iron Teeth Grease (Grease Factory: Extract + Canola Oil) and the Chemical Works recipe was removed. The good stays defined, unproduced and unused, only so saves that hold it still load; a saved Chemical Works set to the old recipe loads with no recipe (native Manufactory.Load).

migratedGoods.$comment: Goods removed with native save migration (user decision 2026-10-30, bricks: "for every item we add, lets remove low value items from the game"). Each removed good is deleted from the data; its id is listed in the GoodSpec.BackwardCompatibleIds of a remaining good of the same storage type, so native GoodService.BindGoodToItsBackwardCompatibleIds resolves a saved stack, cost or reservation of the old id to that good (Timberborn.Goods 1.1.2.8; a saved id nothing resolves is dropped as obsolete). type is the removed good's GoodType, which its target must share. The generators read this table; nothing else lists the mapping (tools/good_migrations.mjs, checked by tools/validate_good_migrations.mjs).

Aggregate.why: Crushed sandstone; concrete now takes sandstone rubble directly and the crusher grinds dirt (brick earth). Not Dirt: Dirt is Pileable and would land in Box warehouses.

Flux.why: Single-recipe Steel Mill intermediate; limestone is the real steelmaking flux and now goes into high-grade steel itself.

Compost.why: Single-recipe intermediate made and used in the Fertilizer Works; the works now make fertilizer in one step.

MedicalFood.why: Plain Hunger 0.3 food with no medical effect; the Hospital uses Medicine.

EmergencyRation.why: Plain Hunger 0.3 food from corn and logs, a duplicate of the vanilla corn ration.

PackagedFood.why: Near-duplicate of canned fish (both Hunger 0.3); the Technical School's flight course now takes canned fish and the grocery stocks eggplant rations.

ArchiveData.why: Single-recipe intermediate whose two consumers were in Mission Control; guidance computers and telemetry now read the recovered artifacts' drives directly, the record caches give artifacts and the chapters count artifacts.

migratedRecipes.$comment: Recipes removed with the goods above. Each id is listed in the RecipeSpec.BackwardCompatibleIds of the recipe that replaces it in the same building, so a manufactory saved on the old recipe loads on the new one (native Manufactory.Load, Timberborn.Workshops 1.1.2.8).

prohibitedConceptDisposition: Legacy development placeholders. Replace DiningService with worker-served native food consumption; replace license goods with persistent education/research state. Do not delete goods from existing saves without an explicit migration (migratedGoods).
validation: Count only authored, reachable blueprint consumers as implemented. Planned uses stay separate and never satisfy the release check. Rocket-specific goods and directly edible foods may have one real use, never zero.
